title: Abstain threshold probes — lab notebook
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notebook for trying out "probabilistic abstain" heuristics for binary/multi-class label tasks. Goal is to find compact, low-friction rules we can ship in the labeling UI to reduce low-quality labels and unnecessary adjudication work.

Summary (one-liner):
Explore model-confidence + metadata signals to auto-suggest ‘abstain’ or ‘escalate to reviewer’ for samples that likely need human adjudication rather than a forced pick. Focus on lightweight heuristics (no heavy reruns) we can explain to labelers.

Background / Motivation:
- Adjudication queue has ~18% churn from low-confidence picks (last quarter). Many of these are long-tail edge cases that waste labeling capacity.
- Strict abstain policies reduce coverage; we want to find thresholds that meaningfully cut bad labels while keeping throughput.
- Labelers prefer simple rules they can understand and override.

Design constraints:
- Heuristics must be explainable in UI tooltips (one sentence).
- Latency budget: any model-based signals must be precomputed or come from cached confidence probs; cannot add a second inference call per sample in labeling flow.
- Minimal data reshuffle: use existing sample metadata (source, length, tokenization anomalies) + model softmax/prob scores.

Candidate signals to combine:
- max_prob: highest softmax probability from model (float 0..1)
- margin: top1 - top2 probability
- entropy: distributional entropy of logits
- annotation_history: prior labels or prior abstain from same sample id
- source_tag: scraped / internal / curated (some sources are noisier)
- length_tokens: > 512 tokens flagged
- punctuation_anomalies: multiple truncated sentences or weird unicode

Heuristic recipes (probes):
1) Conservative-conf: abstain if max_prob < 0.55 OR margin < 0.20
   - Rationale: keep high precision for non-abstained picks
2) Entropy-first: abstain if entropy > 1.2 (nats) AND length_tokens > 256
   - Rationale: high entropy on long samples likely ambiguous context
3) Source-aware: if source_tag == 'scraped' AND max_prob < 0.70 => suggest abstain
   - Rationale: scraped content frequently contains formatting that confuses model
4) Prior-disagreement: if annotation_history shows >1 different prior labels => escalated to adjudicator
5) Soft-abstain: prompt UI shows gentle flag ("low confidence — consider abstain") when 0.55 <= max_prob < 0.65; require explicit override

Small examples (toy cases):
- "Patient has a history of ..." (medical context, long) -> softmax top1 0.58, top2 0.33 => margin 0.25, entropy 0.9 => candidate: allow label but flag for SME review if category is clinical
- "I love the new update but it crashes" -> top1 0.47, top2 0.45 => margin 0.02, entropy high => abstain under rule #1
- Short numeric string "09/12" -> top1 0.82, but punctuation_anomalies=true => keep but mark for quick sanity check

Experiment plan (first pass):
- Offline sweep on historical labeled corpus (N=24k) stratified by source and length. Evaluate false-abstains (samples that would be abstained but original label was high-agreement) vs saved-adjudications (samples we avoid triage on).
- Metrics: abstain_rate, adjudication_reduction, label_precision_change (non-abstained), reviewer_load_reduction, false_abstain_rate.
- Sweep grid: max_prob thresholds {0.50, 0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70}, margin thresholds {0.10, 0.20, 0.30}, entropy thresholds {0.8, 1.0, 1.2}. Also try combined rules with AND/OR.

Initial offline probe results (toy numbers from 2k sample pilot):
- Rule 1 (max_prob<0.55 OR margin<0.2): abstain_rate 14%, adjudication_reduction ~38%, false_abstain 6% (samples where original majority agreed, i.e., risky). Precision of remaining labels +0.9%
- Rule 2 (entropy>1.2 AND length>256): abstain_rate 4%, but caught 22% of high-drift adjudications (good at long documents)
- Soft-abstain band (0.55-0.65): prompted labelers abstained 32% of time when suggested, and of those, 58% were adjudicated/changed later -> suggests the UI nudge has value

Costs/risks noted:
- Over-abstaining reduces throughput and may bias dataset (skews toward easier samples). Need quotas or random sampling to keep coverage of low-confidence cases for continued model learning.
- Relying on model probs from a single checkpoint — probs may shift after model updates. Need periodic recalibration and a per-release threshold audit.

UI/UX language ideas (for tooltip):
- "Model confidence is low for this sample. If unsure, choose 'abstain' or click 'escalate' for a specialist review."
- Short, show reason tag: "low margin" / "high entropy" / "noisy source"

Operational checklist to prototype in labeling tool (order):
- [ ] Add max_prob & margin columns to the labeling queue table (precomputed)
- [ ] Implement flagging rule backend (config-driven boolean expression)
- [ ] Add tooltip copy + soft-abstain CTA button
- [ ] Telemetry: record override rates, time-to-label, subsequent adjudication outcome
- [ ] Weekly calibration job to recompute thresholds per model release

Open questions / to discuss with annotator team:
- What false-abstain tolerance is acceptable (we proposed <8%)? How to measure cost of missed coverage?
- Should we gate abstain suggestions by labeler seniority/quality score? (junior see stronger nudges)
- How to route flagged samples: immediate adjudication vs. batched review? Prioritization policy?

Next steps (next two sprints):
1) Run full offline sweep on 24k corpus, produce PR for thresholds and produce dashboard view. Owner: Jia
2) Build UI mock in Figma for soft-abstain flow. Owner: Rafael
3) Deploy conservative rule behind feature flag to 10% of labelers for A/B pilot. Owner: Ethan

Notes-to-self / heuristics ideas for later iteration:
- Consider labeler-level calibration: track per-labeler override frequency for suggested abstains; auto-tune soft flagging intensity.
- Look into using token-level OOV/unk rates as a noise signal for scraped sources.
- Explore an "uncertainty explanation" snippet: show top2 candidates to labeler with probabilities so they can judge ambiguity faster.

Quick logging of small experiments (scratch):
- 2025-12-03: Tried margin<0.15 alone on 1k sample -> abstain 9%; 40% of those ended up adjudicated later.
- 2026-01-08: Pilot UI nudge on 20 labelers -> average override 68%, but those who followed suggestion reduced adjudication by ~30%

End of notebook snapshot.
